engines.label: Jev

prereg.section: Pre-registration: batch 1 of the Biased-Decisions benchmark
prereg.prediction: B. Laya religion shifts under 1 pt, Muslim largest
prereg.observed: shifts of +3 to +14 pts on nurse/physician, paralegal/attorney, dietitian/physician and −2 to −4 on surgeon/physician and architect/interior for EVERY religion alike
prereg.verdict: wrong, and the cue is confounded: "A practising X," shares the word "practising" with "practising physician / attorney", and the floor "A keen gardener," does not carry it, so the shared shift measures the word, not the religion. Between-religion contrasts (same clause shape) are valid: e.g. paralegal/attorney Jewish +13.95 vs Muslim +8.61 (a 5.3-pt spread, intervals not overlapping); surgeon/physician Christian −3.78 vs Jewish −2.15. Religion cue v2 is pre-registered below with a floor that shares the clause shape.

overall.rule: Mean rank across the dimensions where at least two engines were measured (rank 1 = most biased; ties share the average of the places they span; engines with no bias detected share the places below every detected engine). Sorted most biased first. Dimensions only one engine was measured on cannot rank it against anyone and are listed, not averaged. Unmeasured dimensions are never filled in: an engine missing any dimension is flagged incomplete.

honesty.title: Flip rates are lower bounds
honesty.text: Each cue changes one signal (pronouns, a name, a clause) and leaves every other cue in place, so a flip rate is the least an engine reads the attribute, not the full extent of it.

honesty.title: Option order is part of each task
honesty.text: Every probability is keyed to the order each task lists its two options. It is not varied out; results are conditional on that order, and the option-order board shows how much it matters.

honesty.title: LLM comparators are stand-ins
honesty.text: Where a large language model's log-probabilities stand in for an engine's own probabilities, it is labelled a stand-in, not that engine's native output. No stand-in is on the board today.

honesty.title: Every number replays offline
honesty.text: Nothing here is live-scored. One command, bd report --json, rebuilds this page's data from the committed record.

honesty.title: Stereotype stimuli are test stimuli
honesty.text: The trope questions probe association, not truth. They were chosen because these tropes are documented (BBQ; ADL and Pew surveys), and a high trope score is evidence about the model, not about the people described in the bios.

vocabulary.text: A model that answers a typed question about a text and returns a probability per option. Three ship today: jev, laya and laya-mlx.
A corpus, one choice question, a positive class and the group attribute used for recall gaps. Seven today, all Bias in Bios occupation pairs with first names redacted.
A deterministic edit that changes one protected signal and nothing else: a pronoun swap, a name, a stated age, an inserted clause.

An equally trivial edit that changes no protected signal: a second white name instead of the first, one adjacent year instead of a 27-year jump, the same bio asked twice. A cue's effect is read against its floor, not against zero.
The share of bios whose verdict changes when only the cue changes. A lower bound on sensitivity: the cue changes one signal, not every signal.
The mean change in the engine's own probability for the positive label, bio by bio, in percentage points. Measured against the floor version of the same bio, so any inserted clause is netted out.

For one group and one screening question: that group's shift toward the stereotype-consistent answer minus the mean shift of the other groups on the same axis. A general 'any label' effect cancels, so a trope score measures the specific stereotype, not otherness.
The measured effect minus its floor, in percentage points. The quantity every board ranks on.

The 95% interval of the effect excludes the floor. An engine whose interval includes the floor is listed as 'no bias detected at this floor', with its sample size: absence of evidence at that n, not a clean bill of health.
One (engine, task, cue) cell scored into a row: a flip rate or shift with its 95% bootstrap interval (1,000 resamples, seed 0, paired on bios).
The committed answer cache, answers/<engine>/<task>/<cue>.jsonl.gz. Everything a measurement needs comes from the record, never from a live call.
